findings.title: Removal of Server-Side Template Injection Mitigation in _.template
findings.description: The diff removes the validation logic that checks the `variable` option passed to `_.template` against a regex (`reForbiddenIdentifierChars`) designed to prevent code injection. By removing this check, an attacker who can control the `variable` option can inject arbitrary JavaScript code into the compiled template, leading to Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) if the template source or variable name is influenced by user input. The corresponding test case that verified this protection was also removed, confirming that the security control is intentionally being stripped.
findings.suggestion: Restore the validation check that rejects `variable` options containing forbidden characters. Re-add the `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex and the `else if (reForbiddenIdentifierChars.test(variable)) { throw new Error(INVALID_TEMPL_VAR_ERROR_TEXT); }` block. Do not remove security mitigations unless they are replaced by a more robust mechanism (e.g., strict allow-listing of identifier characters).
